acceptance: Two agents in one Claude Code session can each hold a claim at the same time, or the tool refuses with a message naming the holding agent and how to wait
A claim taken by one agent cannot be finished or released by another agent without takeover
A test covers two agents on one server
context: Found 2026-10-17 during the site-split remediation; the error text is in that session's transcript. The coordinator's workaround was to retry until the shared slot was free. todo-db source: ~/Developer/todo-db (src/todo_db/service.py has the same check at the same lines).
description:
The tracker allows one live claim per worker (vendored todo_db 0.9.1, todo_db/service.py:933-943 raises E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS). The MCP server derives the worker identity once per server process when --actor and TODO_DB_ACTOR are unset (todo_db/mcp/server.py:45,75,106). Every subagent of one Claude Code session talks to the same server, so they all act as one worker, `mcp:claude-code:joe@joe-mac-mini.local:0f148a36cca5316266af272c`.

On 2026-10-17 a site-split agent's take on site-split-50 and site-split-55 failed with E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS at least 12 times, because unrelated agents in the same session held claims on spark-tuning-discovery-cli, spark-effective-config-preflight-capture, spark-family-session-config-velox-lakesail and tuning-render-layout-postgres-family-20261001. Those agents could finish and release each other's work, so claim ownership did not protect anything either.

Give each agent its own worker identity, for example a per-call agent or session id that becomes part of the worker, or document and enforce one claim per session with a clear recovery hint naming the holder.
